Meeting your specs, exceeding your expectations. 1201 East Oak St, Louisville, KY 40204 (502) 714 - 7200 info@occamdesign.com A division of CreoSalus, Inc About Our Team Testimonials Capabilities Capabilities Our Experience Contact Us Resources White Papers Blog Funding Resources Media Careers About Our Team Testimonials Capabilities Capabilities Our Experience Contact Us Resources White Papers Blog Funding Resources Media Careers The medical device sector is a rapidly-evolving landscape with clear trends emerging that will dominate the industry for 2025. Innovations like AI and expanding sectors like 3D printing, remote device monitoring, and device connectivity are all emerging as integral considerations for medical device manufacturers and users alike.

Forward thinking is the only way to effectively compete in the medical device market, and Occam Design combines a driving interest in innovation with ISO 13485:2016 certification, FDA registration, and 30+ years of industry experience to remain a key player in medical device development and manufacturing.

Market Growth and Sector Expansion The medical device market is growing steadily, owing to a driving desire for healthcare options that are more cost effective, have a greater health impact, and serve growing needs for medical device support.
The global market for smart medical devices, both therapeutic and diagnostic, was 90.55 billion in 2024, and is expected to grow 12.84% in 2025.
Reasons behind this growth include: An aging population with an increasing demand for supportive medical devices.

Key Innovations Shaping the Market Cybersecurity As medical devices increasingly become part of the “internet of things” their connectivity transmits important and confidential medical data across devices.

Protecting the safety of patients through preemptive cybersecurity measures built in to device design and development is not only important, but a regulatory requirement to ensure a device can go to market.
Artificial Intelligence (AI) AI expedites processing large amounts of information, helping medical professionals find trends and outliers in patient data with a previously unknown rapidity.
Alongside helping patients and care professionals, AI also speeds up automation and process workflows, allowing device developers to create more efficient and proactive devices and equipment.

Devices can be fit and then custom printed to an individual, and the rapidity of both prototyping and manufacturing has fast-tracked medical device development, allowing device designers to meet needs more efficiently.

Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) When patients’ healthcare data can be monitored both continuously and remotely more rapid healthcare support can be offered when metrics change, particularly for patients with chronic disease or intensive care needs, like cardiac patients.

Remote patient monitoring (RPM) devices also allow healthcare systems to leverage and expand telehealth and virtual care efforts, helping medical care reach more people in effective and affordable ways.

Medical Trends to Watch Medical device trends through 2025 embrace technology as a tremendous source of opportunity for reshaping patient care through improvement of patient comfort and outcomes, as well as making healthcare delivery both more straightforward, and more effective.
